verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Week-Ahead: Into a Triple Gauntlet — SPCX Supply, CPI June 10, Iran — Before Warsh
verdict.rationale_short: Markets are closed (Sunday). This is a forward-looking week-ahead briefing positioning into the June 8 open, after a week that broke the framework (Friday NFP 172K, SPX through 7,460, VIX ~20.9) and a weekend of US-Iran strikes near Hormuz. The defensive posture stays STEP ASIDE because the week front-loads three sequential risks into the most hostile regime of the series: the SPCX roadshow opens Monday (a ~$75B liquidity drain at a fixed $135), May CPI lands Wednesday June 10 as the decisive inflation binary, and the Iran escalation is an open-ended oil/geopolitical tail — all before the Warsh FOMC on June 16-17. The plan is capital preservation: hold cash, keep the IWM short into the SPCX drain, hedge the Iran oil tail, and let CPI — not the dip — decide when to re-engage.

supporting_data.label: SPCX roadshow opens Monday June 8 — SpaceX set a fixed $135/share for 556.6M shares, ~$75B raise at a ~$1.75-1.77T valuation (the largest IPO in history); pricing June 11, Nasdaq debut June 12; the liquidity drain begins this week

May CPI releases Wednesday June 10 — consensus near 4.2% YoY headline with a milder core (+0.2% m/m vs April's +0.4%); a hot print confirms the higher-for-longer break and makes the June 17 Warsh FOMC a live hike; the S&P is vulnerable to a CPI surprise after Friday's break

Iran tail open-ended: US and Iran exchanged strikes near Hormuz over the weekend, with Iran calling the US action a 'flagrant violation' of the ceasefire; a Pakistani-mediated channel is deadlocked over $24B in frozen Iranian assets — an unresolved oil/geopolitical risk into the week
Last close (Fri June 5): SPX 7,383.74 (-2.64%, below the 7,460 floor), Nasdaq 25,709.43 (-4.18%), VIX ~20.9, 30Y 5.007%, 10Y 4.544%; semis worst since March 2020
Crypto remains broken into the week: BTC bottomed near ~$59,227 and ETH below $1,900 over the weekend; ~$390B erased — cross-asset confirmation that risk appetite has reset, not rotated

Warsh FOMC June 16-17 is the week's terminal event — after the hot jobs print, the 10Y at 4.54% reflects concern the Fed must tame a hot economy; CPI June 10 sets the tone for whether June 17 is a hawkish hold or a live hike

bear_case: The week-ahead risk is that the market has to absorb three sequential blows before it can even reach the Warsh FOMC, and it enters them already broken. Monday brings the start of a ~$75B SPCX liquidity drain; Wednesday brings a CPI that consensus already sees rising toward 4.2% headline; and the Iran conflict — now featuring active US-Iran strikes near Hormuz — is an open-ended oil tail that directly threatens the inflation print and the Fed's hand. The S&P enters this gauntlet below its 7,460 floor with the VIX above 20, the 30Y back above 5.0%, the semis fresh off their worst day since March 2020, and crypto down ~$390B — a tape with no cushion and no clear catalyst to stop the bleed before CPI. If CPI runs hot on June 10, the June 17 FOMC becomes a live hike, the 30Y targets 5.10-5.20%, and SPX 7,250 is the next real support. Invalidation level: a cool CPI (core ≤0.2% m/m) with the 30Y back below 5.0% and VIX below 18 restores a HOLD and reopens NVDA ($200-206) and selective longs; a hot CPI with the 30Y above 5.05%, or an SPX close below 7,300, converts STEP ASIDE to bearish — stay defensive and let the FOMC clear before re-risking.
